items.title: BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra issues apology to law students after NALSAR convocation row
items.summary: Bar Council of India (BCI) chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra has issued an apology to law students in a letter issued on Independence Day. The apology follows criticism from students at National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (NALSAR) University of Law at Hyderabad and National Law School of India University (NLSIU) Bangalore over BCI's handling of the row surrounding Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant's participation in NALSAR's 2026 convocation. Though the apology does not name the university or dispute directly, it refers to recent developments which he said had caused concern among students. "If anything connected with the present controversy, any of my words, or letter, has hurt the feelings of our law students, I sincerely regret and apologise for the same. There should be no hesitation in saying so. An expression of regret is not a matter of prestige or ego. It is simply an acknowledgment that the feelings and concerns of our students matter," the statement said. The controversy began after the BCI on August 13 ordered a halt on the enrolment for NALSAR's graduating batch of 2026 for objecting to the participation of CJI Surya Kant as the chief guest for their convo

items.title: After barring, backtracking and an inquiry u-turn, BCI chief apologises to NALSAR students
items.summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman and BJP leader Manan Kumar Mishra has expressed regret and apologised to law students of NALSAR University of Law, without addressing them specifically. In a statement issued on August 15, Manan Mishra addressed law students as ‘My dear young friends’ and said, “If anything connected with the present controversy, any of my words, or letter, has hurt the feelings of our law students, I sincerely regret and apologise for the same.” “There should be no hesitation in saying so. An expression of regret is not a matter of prestige or ego. It is simply an acknowledgment that the feelings and concerns of our students matter,” he added. The change in tone came about after alumni and students of NALSAR and National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, wrote a letter to the BCI condemning Manan Mishra for his statements and criticising him for clamping down on free speech. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.

items.title: Delimitation: பாஜகவுக்கு எப்படி பலன் கொடுக்கும்? | CM Vijay | BJP | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The debate over delimitation is not only about how many seats a state gains or loses, but also about federalism, political representation and whether population should be the sole basis for determining electoral strength. The 2023 delimitation of Assam has added another dimension to these concerns. Critics have alleged that the exercise diluted the electoral influence of minority voters by concentrating them in fewer constituencies. So, what could a similar exercise mean for Tamil Nadu and other southern states? Is the concern simply about losing constituencies, or is there a larger question about how India’s demographic balance could change? In this week's episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed examines the politics behind delimitation, the concerns of southern states and what the Assam precedent signals the future of electoral representation in India.
